## Context / Problem

The reconciler's outbound status/priority mapper keeps a process-global dedupe set
`_DRIFT_WARNED` (declared at `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_family/outbound_mapper.py:45`)
so a persistently drifting status warns at most once per process. `resolve_outbound_status`
adds a value to that set on first drift (`outbound_mapper.py:63-64`) and suppresses the
stderr warning thereafter. The status-mapping tests in
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_status_mapping.py` never reset that set via an autouse
fixture: only `test_drift_warning_deduped_within_pass` calls
`outbound_mapper.reset_drift_warnings()` (public reset at `outbound_mapper.py:32-39`), and it
does so at its own start. A test that asserts a drift warning IS emitted for a status
(`test_unmapped_status_drifts`, which asserts `"blocked"` reaches stderr) can therefore be
polluted under test reordering: if an earlier test already recorded that status in
`_DRIFT_WARNED`, the dedupe suppresses the warning and the assertion fails. This is
non-manifesting today (CI runs the module green in definition order) but is a latent
order-dependency and purely defensive to fix.

## Approach

Add a module-scoped `autouse` pytest fixture to
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_status_mapping.py` that calls
`outbound_mapper.reset_drift_warnings()` before each test, so every status-mapping test
starts with an empty `_DRIFT_WARNED`. This makes drift-emission assertions order-independent
without changing any production behavior. This approach fits because the pollution is a
shared-mutable-process-state hazard scoped entirely to this test module; the codebase already
exposes `reset_drift_warnings()` as the sanctioned reset entry point (used by the existing
dedupe test), so the fixture reuses that public seam rather than reaching into the private
set. A fixture is the idiomatic pytest mechanism for per-test state isolation and is strictly
narrower than resetting globally.

## Scope

- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_status_mapping.py` — add one `autouse` fixture calling
  `outbound_mapper.reset_drift_warnings()`, and add a two-part order-independence oracle
  (one test that records a drift for `blocked` in the shared set, a second that asserts the
  `blocked` drift warning still fires despite that prior record — passing only because the
  fixture cleared the set between tests).

No production source changes: `outbound_mapper.py` already provides
`reset_drift_warnings()`; this is a test-only, behavior-preserving change.

## Testing

- RED first: with the autouse fixture ABSENT, the second oracle test fails for the right
  reason — the prior test's record of `blocked` in `_DRIFT_WARNED` suppresses the warning, so
  the `"blocked" in stderr` assertion fails.
- GREEN: adding the autouse fixture clears `_DRIFT_WARNED` before each test, so the warning
  fires and the assertion passes regardless of ordering.
- Teeth: temporarily removing the fixture returns the oracle to RED, proving the fixture is
  load-bearing.
- Full module stays green: `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_status_mapping.py`.
- Assertions target OBSERVABLE behavior (the stderr drift warning), never the private set's
  contents. No timing/wall-clock assertions are added.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] An `autouse` fixture in `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_status_mapping.py` calls
  `outbound_mapper.reset_drift_warnings()` before each test in the module.
- [x] A two-part oracle demonstrates order-independence: it is RED (the drift warning is
  suppressed) when the fixture is absent and GREEN when present, verified by temporarily
  removing the fixture.
- [x] `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_status_mapping.py` passes.
- [x] `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass (ruff check + format-check + complexity ratchet +
  wall-clock-assert gate + module-size gate; mypy).
- [x] No production source files change; `outbound_mapper.py` is untouched.
